title: Merge two sorted arrays without extra space
stepTitle: Solve Problems on Arrays [Easy -> Medium -> Hard]
category: Solve Problems on Arrays [Easy -> Medium -> Hard]
problemStatement: Merge two sorted arrays in-place, with O(1) extra space.
intuition: Treat the two arrays as one virtual array of length n+m. The gap method repeatedly compares elements a fixed distance apart and halves the gap — exactly Shell sort restricted to already-sorted halves.

approaches.title: Brute: merge into a third array
approaches.code:
def merge_extra(a: list[int], b: list[int]) -> None:
    merged = sorted(a + b)
    a[:] = merged[: len(a)]
    b[:] = merged[len(a):]
approaches.time: O((n+m) log(n+m)) with sort, O(n+m) with a real merge

approaches.title: Better: swap-and-sort (O(1) space)
approaches.idea: Swap out-of-order pairs across the boundary, then re-sort both halves.
approaches.code:
def merge_swap(a: list[int], b: list[int]) -> None:
    i, j = len(a) - 1, 0
    while i >= 0 and j < len(b) and a[i] > b[j]:
        a[i], b[j] = b[j], a[i]
        i -= 1
        j += 1
    a.sort()
    b.sort()
approaches.time: O(n log n + m log m)

approaches.title: Optimal: gap method
approaches.idea: gap = ceil((n+m)/2), halve each round, compare elements gap apart in the virtual array.
approaches.dryRun:
a=[1,4,8,10] b=[2,3,9] total=7 gap=4
compare (0,4),(1,5),(2,6) and swap where needed
gap 2, then 1, then stop -> a=[1,2,3,4] b=[8,9,10]
approaches.whyWorks: Each gap pass fixes all inversions at that distance; halving down to 1 leaves the virtual array sorted.

specialTechnique.title: Gap (Shell) method
specialTechnique.body: Use ceil when halving the gap, and stop after the gap-1 pass. Getting gap = 1 but never running it is the classic off-by-one.

edgeCases: All of b smaller than all of a
commonMistakes: Halving with floor, which skips the final gap-1 pass
Mixing up index mapping in the virtual array
patternRecognition: "In-place merge" -> gap method; "extra space allowed" -> plain two-pointer merge
followUps: LeetCode 88 variant where a has trailing space (merge from the back)
interviewInsight: Present all three tiers. The gap method is the differentiator but the back-to-front merge is what LeetCode 88 wants.
